class.name: SandWorld
class.brief_description: High-performance cellular automata sandbox simulation engine using sparse chunk grid.
class.description: SandWorld is a GDExtension providing a falling sand simulation engine optimized for Godot 4.x. It uses: - Flat memory layout with 64x64 pixel chunks - Dynamic data-driven material configurations and reaction rules - Sparse chunked world grid for large landscapes - Direct texture rendering via PackedByteArray Features SOLID_POWDER, LIQUID and GAS physics, configurable reactions between materials, and interactive brushes. A new world starts with a built-in set of materials (Stone, Sand, Water, Acid, Fire, Smoke, Wood, Burning Wood, Ash, Gravel, Steam, Oil, Lava), so it can be painted immediately. See [method get_default_materials_json] for their IDs and settings. Registering your own materials replaces them.

method.name: add_material
method.description: Register a material type with this world ([param id] 1-255; 0 is empty). Materials are per-world. The first material registered on a new world removes all built-in default materials and reactions; call [method load_default_materials] first to extend them instead. State values: 0=EMPTY, 1=SOLID_FIXED, 2=SOLID_POWDER, 3=LIQUID, 4=GAS. Density determines sinking/floating for SOLID_POWDER/LIQUID (higher sinks); for GAS it inverts, so lower density rises past denser gas/fluid. Dispersion is how many empty cells a liquid/gas can slide sideways per tick. decay_chance is the 0-255 per-tick probability this material converts into decay_into (e.g. Fire decaying into Smoke); 0 disables decay. Interactions with other materials are defined with [method add_reaction].

method.name: add_reaction
method.description: Register a reaction: each tick, a cell of [param material] touching (8-neighborhood) a cell of [param other] has a [param chance]/256 probability (1-255) of turning into [param material_into] while the neighbor turns into [param other_into]. Pass the original ID to leave a cell unchanged, or 0 to remove it. Rules are checked in registration order. Reaction products can't react again in the same tick. [codeblock] world.add_reaction(SAND, FIRE, FIRE, FIRE, 120) # sand catches fire world.add_reaction(STONE, ACID, 0, ACID, 80) # acid dissolves stone world.add_reaction(FIRE, WATER, SMOKE, WATER, 200) # water puts out fire [/codeblock]

method.name: apply_impulse
method.description: Push every powder and liquid particle within [param radius] of [param pos] away from it, adding [param strength] cells per tick to its velocity at the center, falling off linearly to 0 just past the radius. Particles at the center are pushed straight up. Fixed solids and gases are not affected. Pushed particles fly in arcs under [member gravity] and slow down by their material's friction once they land.

method.name: get_particle_velocity
method.description: Velocity of the particle at [param pos] in cells per tick (+y is down), or [code]Vector2.ZERO[/code] for an empty cell. Velocities are stored in steps of 1/16 cell per tick, up to about 7.9 in each direction.

method.name: set_particle_velocity
method.description: Set the velocity of the particle at [param pos] in cells per tick (+y is down). Does nothing on an empty cell. Only powders and liquids move by their velocity.

method.name: brush_circle
method.description: Fill a circular area with particles of the specified material.

method.name: brush_line
method.description: Draw a line of particles with circular brush from point to point using Bresenham's algorithm.

method.name: brush_rectangle
method.description: Fill a rectangular area with particles of the specified material.

method.name: clear
method.description: Clear all particles from the simulation. Materials and reactions are kept.

method.name: clear_reactions
method.description: Remove every reaction registered with [method add_reaction].

method.name: load_snapshot
method.description: Replace the world with a snapshot created by [method save_snapshot]. Material IDs are remapped by the names given to [method add_material], so register the same named materials before loading. Returns [code]false[/code] (and prints the reason) when the data has an invalid or unsupported format, or uses a material name that is not registered; the existing world is left unchanged.

method.name: damage_circle
method.description: Deal [param amount] damage to every particle in a circular area. See [method damage_particle].

method.name: damage_particle
method.description: Deal [param amount] damage to the particle at [param pos]. If the damage is less than its hp, the hp is reduced and 0 is returned. Otherwise the particle breaks into its material's break_into (see [method set_materials_from_dict]) and the leftover damage is returned (breaking costs its hp, at least 1). An empty cell returns [param amount] unchanged. The return value lets a projectile keep going: spend the leftover on the next cell along its path, and stop when it reaches 0. To test whether something can penetrate a cell without damaging it, compare its power with [method get_particle_hp].

method.name: explosion
method.description: Damage particles in a circular area. Damage is [param power] at the center, falls off linearly with distance, and is at least 1 inside the radius, so materials with max_hp 0 are always destroyed. Particles whose hp is exhausted turn into their material's break_into. See [method damage_particle]. Then flings loose material (powders and liquids, including debris the blast just broke off) within twice the radius outward, as [method apply_impulse] with a strength of up to 5 cells per tick at power 255.

method.name: get_default_materials_json
method.description: Return the JSON of the built-in default materials every new world starts with, in the format accepted by [method load_materials_json]. Useful as a template for your own material files.

method.name: get_chunk_count
method.description: Return the number of active chunks in the world.

method.name: get_debug_chunk_info
method.description: Return one Dictionary per allocated chunk, for debug visualization. Each entry has: - "chunk_position" (Vector2i): the chunk's coordinates. - "world_rect" (Rect2i): the chunk's 64x64 bounds in world (pixel) coordinates. - "dirty_rect" (Rect2i): world-space bounds of the cells pending simulation next tick. Zero-sized if the chunk is currently asleep.

method.name: get_particle_hp
method.description: Get the remaining hp (0-255) of the particle at the given position, or 0 if empty. Particles start at their material's max_hp.

method.name: get_particle_mat_id
method.description: Get the material ID of the particle at the given position, or 0 if empty.

method.name: load_default_materials
method.description: Replace all materials and reactions with the built-in defaults (see [method get_default_materials_json]). Unlike on a new world, materials registered afterwards are added to the defaults instead of replacing them.

method.name: load_materials_json
method.description: Register materials from a JSON object keyed by material ID, with the same keys as [method set_materials_from_dict] and colors given as HTML strings such as [code]"#e6d899"[/code]. Returns [code]false[/code] if the text is not a JSON object. [codeblock] world.load_materials_json(FileAccess.get_file_as_string("res://materials.json")) [/codeblock]

method.name: render_to_texture
method.description: Render simulation to RGBA8888 PackedByteArray. Can be used with Image.set_data() or ImageTexture.update().

method.name: set_materials_from_dict
method.description: Bulk register materials from a dictionary. On a new world this first removes the built-in default materials (see [method add_material]). Each key is material ID (an int, or a numeric String as produced by JSON), value is a dict with keys: name, state, color (a Color or an HTML color String), density, dispersion, decay_chance, decay_into (see [method add_material]), plus these optional per-particle keys (all 0-255, default 0): - max_hp: hp a new particle starts with. Damage from [method damage_particle], [method explosion] and damaging reactions reduces it. 0 means any damage breaks the particle. - hp_loss_chance: per-tick probability (out of 256) of losing 1 hp, giving the material a lifetime (e.g. burning wood with max_hp 60). - break_into: material ID the particle becomes when its hp is exhausted, by damage or over time; 0 destroys it. - color_variation: maximum brightness offset applied per particle when rendering, from a random shade fixed when the particle is created. - friction: share (out of 256) of a powder's or liquid's sideways speed lost each tick while it rests on something. 0 slides until it hits a wall; higher values stop thrown sand or splashing liquid sooner. If present, reactions is an Array of Dictionaries with keys other, chance, into (defaults to the material itself), other_into (defaults to other) and damage (defaults to 0), and replaces that material's existing reactions. With a non-zero damage, each successful roll takes that much hp from the neighbor instead of converting it, and the neighbor becomes its own break_into (not other_into) once its hp is exhausted. See [method add_reaction]. [codeblock] world.set_materials_from_dict({ 1: { "name": "Stone", "state": 1, "color": Color("808080"), "density": 100, "max_hp": 120, "break_into": 7, "color_variation": 12 }, 4: { "name": "Acid", "state": 3, "color": Color("78d83d"), "density": 45, "dispersion": 3, "reactions": [{ "other": 1, "chance": 80, "damage": 20 }] }, }) [/codeblock]

method.name: save_snapshot
method.description: Return a versioned binary snapshot of the current sparse world. Snapshot data includes allocated chunks and each particle's material ID, flags, hp, shade and velocity, but not material definitions. Snapshots from before velocity was added still load, with every particle at rest; older ones are rejected.

method.name: set_seed
method.description: Seed this world's random number generator. The same seed, materials and initial particles produce the same simulation.

method.name: set_particle
method.description: Place a particle of the specified material at the given position, with its material's max_hp and a random shade.

method.name: tick
method.description: Advance simulation by one frame. Call this in _process() or _physics_process() for continuous simulation.

members.member: Speed in cells per tick that an unsupported powder or liquid particle gains each tick. Falling particles move at least 1 cell per tick even at 0, as without velocity. Stored in steps of 1/16, up to about 7.9.
Fastest a particle can fall, in cells per tick (1 to about 7.9). Fast particles still stop at the first obstacle on their path rather than passing through it.

constants.constant: Fixed solid (stone, brick) - does not move.
Powder (sand, gunpowder) - falls under gravity, keeps momentum, and piles up.
Liquid (water, oil, acid) - falls under gravity, splashes, and flows sideways until level, then settles so still pools stop simulating.
Gas (smoke, steam, fire) - rises and disperses.
